issues.detail: The Greek 'επεπεσεν αυτω' (epepesen autō) means 'fell upon him' (the person). The Vietnamese 'té trên người' means 'fell on [his] body/person'. While close, the Vietnamese phrasing 'té trên người' can be interpreted as falling *on top of* someone's body as a physical location, whereas the Greek implies falling *upon* the person in an action of embracing/seizing. However, a more significant issue is the lack of clarity regarding 'autō'. In this context (Acts 20:34), 'autō' refers to the man who fell. The Vietnamese 'té trên người' is ambiguous as to whose body it is (could be interpreted as his own body or the other's).
